chunks: Aban narrated from Abu al-‘Abbas, from Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who said: “My slave is free, and he must perform such-and-such labor for such-and-such a year.” He said: “He is free, and the labor is upon him.”

I said: “Ibn Abi Layla claims that he is free and that nothing is upon him.” He said: “He has lied. Indeed, ‘Ali عليه السلام freed Aba Nayzar, ‘Iyadan, and Riyahan, while labor for such-and-such a number of years was upon them, and they had their provision and their clothing in a reasonable manner during those years.”

key_terms.السِّنِينَ: the specified years of the obligation
key_terms.بِالْمَعْرُوفِ: according to what is fair and customary
key_terms.عُمَالَةُ: a labor obligation or required service

ai.seo_question: Can a freed slave remain obligated to work for a fixed number of years after manumission in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a slave may be freed while still being bound to a stipulated term of labor. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rejects the contrary view and cites the precedent of Imam ‘Ali عليه السلام, who emancipated individuals under such a condition while ensuring their provision and clothing according to what was reasonable.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3475 - Aban narrated from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

I asked him about a man who said: "My slave is free, but he must work for me for such-and-such a number of years."
Imam (as) said: "He is free, but he is obligated to fulfill the work."

I said: "Ibn Abi Layla claims that he is free and is not obligated to do anything."
Imam (as) said: "He has lied! Indeed, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) freed Abu Nayzar, 'Iyad, and Riah, while requiring them to work for such-and-such a number of years. They were provided with their sustenance and clothing in a reasonable manner during those years."
